subject: Immediate hotpatch: routing failover & latency mitigation
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acmepay.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 23 Aug 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate hotpatch: routing failover & latency mitigation

Jordan —

Quick heads-up: we observed a small but growing class of requests hitting a rare routing path that amplifies tail-latency under high long-context load. We’re seeing a ~10x token latency spike in <0.1% of requests which in turn surfaces as timeouts in some customer integrations (you may have seen 504s).

Action we’re taking right now: we need to push an unscheduled hotpatch to the routing layer to (1) short-circuit the legacy fallback for large-sequence inference, (2) apply an immediate KV-cache affinity fix, and (3) temporarily force affected customers onto the fast-path model variant while we validate the full fix. This work will be performed as a rolling change to avoid cluster-wide restarts.

Planned window: 2028-08-23 18:00–18:20 PDT (can be shortened). Expected customer impact: small number of requests may see 5–10s increased latency during their first request following the affinity flip; overall error rates should decrease. We will NOT be taking the API down.

I’ve attached the hotfix README and the short remediation plan. Please let me know if you need us to pause — otherwise we’ll proceed at the window above. I’ve copied our account team to coordinate any contractual/credit questions.

Karthik
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: hotfix_readme_v1.pdf (summary of change), routing_remediation_plan.xlsx (rollout checklist)
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acmepay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmepay.com>, Seth O'Neil <seth.oneil@acmepay.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 23 Aug 2028 16:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate hotpatch: routing failover & latency mitigation

Karthik — thanks for the rapid flag. Appreciate the rollback-safety callouts. Quick questions from our side:

- Will this change affect request ordering or result determinism for ongoing sessions? (We have payment session workflows; determinism matters.)
- If there’s any residual data exposure risk when moving users between model variants, we need confirmation on no cross-tenant KV leakage.
- If this creates elevated errors for us during the window, what is Redwood’s remediation/credit policy? Our procurement team is cc’d.

We’re broadly OK with a short rolling window as long as determinism and data isolation are preserved. Please confirm ASAP so we can communicate to our SREs.

—Jordan
Infrastructure Lead, Acme Payments

Date: Thu, 23 Aug 2028 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate hotpatch: routing failover & latency mitigation

Jordan —

Short answers up front:
- Determinism: the hotpatch forces a routing decision but does not change model weights or decoding. There is no change to sampling seeds; deterministic sessions remain deterministic.
- Isolation: KV cache affinity adjustments are tenant-scoped; we have verified the patch in staging for cross-tenant isolation (no leakage).
- Credits: if you see customer-visible errors above your SLA during this window we will start a credit review automatically; please flag any incidents inside the next 72 hours so we can expedite.

Operational notes: we will notify via the status page at each phase (preflight, start, verification, rollback/complete). Our SRE on-call (Grace) will watch the Telemetry dashboard and can open a private Slack channel with your SREs if useful.

Planned: proceed at 18:00 PDT, rolling across 3 availability zones. We will publish a short postmortem with root cause and mitigations within 48 hours.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate hotpatch: routing failover & latency mitigation

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick confirmation yesterday and for looping procurement. Status update: we completed the rolling hotpatch at 18:09 PDT last night. Key points:

- Incident observed: a legacy routing fallback could be selected for requests with >8k token prefixes when the hot-path was saturated; under those conditions the fallback invoked a non-optimized attention kernel leading to extreme tail latency.
- Rollout: hotpatch applied rolling AZ-by-AZ; no full cluster restarts.
- Customer impact: we saw a transient rise in 5xxs for a small percentage of initial upstream connections during affinity flips (roughly 0.03% of total requests for the hour surrounding the window). Most customers experienced improved P95/P99 after the change.
- Determinism & isolation: validated — no cross-tenant KV leakage, deterministic sessions preserved.

Next steps:
1) Postmortem draft will be published to the Drive link below by EOD.
2) We will run a targeted validation sweep against Acme’s representative workloads this week and share latency curves.
3) If you report any customer-impacting incidents tied to this window we will start the credit evaluation immediately — please open a ticket referencing incident gmi-20280823-ihp-001.

Link to logs & draft postmortem: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b-hotpatch-logs

Appreciate the quick coordination; we’ll follow up with the full write-up shortly.

Karthik
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
